# PART 1 – The claim and credibility {.darkslide background-color="rgba(0,0,0,0)"}

::: {.partlabel}
Part 1
:::

::: notes
Part one, then. We start further back than you might expect, with what science is for, why anyone thinks it is in trouble, and the red-card study, in which twenty-nine teams analysed one dataset and disagreed. Then the vocabulary that separates three kinds of repetition, and the three very large studies, published together, that measured how often social-science findings survive being repeated, one of which supplies the case of today. The part ends on that case: the published experiment that we work on all day, and the claim from it that five analysts reanalysed. Before the break you run the setup check, so that R is ready on your machine for the rest of the day.
:::
